steps.title: Load the quarter's filings
steps.prose: What was asked of government, on the record. After this: one row per filing, and every count downstream is a count of these. Invented data; no real filing.
steps.data_description: Every filing in the sample, as the CSV records it.

steps.title: Load what each client said in public
steps.prose: The promise each ask will be held against. After this: one row per organisation — if one appears twice, every filing for it doubles at the join. Also invented.
steps.data_description: Every organisation with a public commitment on record.

steps.title: Join each filing to its client's commitment
steps.prose: Pairs each ask with the promise it will be read against, without losing an ask. After this: every filing is still here, and a blank commitment means none was on record — an answer, not a gap.
steps.data_description: Every filing, plus its client's commitment where one matched.

steps.title: Read the two texts against each other
steps.prose: Whether an ask contradicts a promise is a reading, and this is where it is made. After this: every filing carries a verdict and the sentence behind it. Trust this step least — check both texts yourself.
steps.data_description: The same filings, plus the model's judgment and its one-sentence note.

steps.title: Flag the contradictions
steps.prose: Turns that reading into something you can count. After this: a filing is flagged only where a promise was on record AND the model called it contradicted, so a missing promise can never read as a clean one.

steps.title: Publish the report
steps.prose: What you hand to someone who was not here — open it under Published, below. After this: one page, every row linked back to the filing it came from.
steps.data_description: One row per filing, as published.
